documentation: Per-track LaTeX warning baselines for the Human Languages books. The books workflow scans each compiled book.log with code/scripts/scan_latex_log_warnings.py and fails a track only when it EXCEEDS the counts recorded here. A track recorded as null has never been measured: it is scanned and reported, never failed. null means 'unknown', NOT 'zero' -- these numbers can only come from a real XeLaTeX run over all 20 books, so they are never guessed.
bootstrap: The first CI run after this file lands prints a copy-paste-ready 'tracks' block of the counts it actually measured into the job summary of the 'Scan book logs for LaTeX warnings' step. Paste that block over the 'tracks' object below to turn the gate on. Lower any number the summary later reports as 'under baseline'; never raise one without explaining why in the commit message.

warningClasses.overfull: Overfull \hbox or \vbox: text spills past the type block.
warningClasses.underfull: Underfull \hbox or \vbox: stretched glue leaves loose lines.
warningClasses.missing_character: A glyph the font does not contain was silently dropped.
warningClasses.hyperref_warning: Package hyperref Warning, usually a broken or unsafe link target.
warningClasses.duplicate_destination: Two PDF destinations share one name, so one link silently wins.
warningClasses.font_substitution: LaTeX substituted a font shape the preamble asked for.

provenance: Seeded 2026-08-11 (HL-C109) from a real XeLaTeX run over all 22 books on macOS (TeX Live 2026, XeTeX via latexmk), driven by code/scripts/build-books-locally.sh, then corrected against CI's own run. Numbers are measured, never guessed. CI is the authority when the two disagree: its Ubuntu TeX Live found one more underfull box than macOS did in russian (0 -> 1) and tamil (1 -> 2), which is a hyphenation-pattern difference between the two distributions and not new damage -- overfull is 0 in every track on both. Take any future disagreement from the job summary the same way. The overfull counts should stay at zero: every one of them was a real page defect and every one was fixed, not silenced. Re-measured 2026-08-11 (HL-C88) after the callout boxes were set ragged right: underfull fell from 24 to 5 across all 22 books (hindi 2, kannada 1, latin 1, telugu 1), and every other track measured 0 locally. russian and tamil are recorded as 1 rather than the 0 measured here, because CI's Ubuntu TeX Live has consistently found one more box than macOS in exactly those two; the baseline is a ceiling, so carrying the known delta avoids failing on a distribution difference. Lower them once a CI run confirms 0. Re-measured 2026-08-11 (HL-C109b) after a slash was made a legal break point: hindi 2 -> 0, and the corpus-wide underfull count fell from 5 to 3 (kannada 1, latin 1, telugu 1). tamil paginates one page shorter (249 -> 248) because a slash run that had been forcing a loose line now breaks; overfull stayed 0 in every track. Re-measured 2026-08-11 (HL-C109c) after opening delimiters stopped blocking hyphenation: latin 1 -> 0, corpus-wide underfull 3 -> 2 (kannada 1, telugu 1, both the same table-of-contents defect). No page count moved and every track built. Re-measured 2026-08-11 (HL-C109d) after over-long section short titles were cut to a width budget: kannada 1 -> 0 and telugu 1 -> 0, and the corpus reaches 0 overfull, 0 underfull and 0 missing characters in all 22 books. russian and tamil stay at 1 rather than 0 for the same reason as before -- CI's Ubuntu TeX Live has consistently found one more box than macOS in exactly those two, and the baseline is a ceiling. Lower them once a CI run confirms 0.
